abstract: A ubiquitous property of physical and biological systems is scale-free dynamics in which spectral power decreases as a function of frequency, showing a 1/f spectral slope. The 1/f slope of neural power spectra has been proposed as a marker of cortical excitation-inhibition (E/I) balance, based on pharmacological experiments and computational models of synaptic activity in cortical networks. However, whether or not the spectral slope in the human population recordings, influenced by biophysical or experimental factors, can be utilized as an index of cortical E/I is debatable. Here, we show that this slope can be volitionally modulated and that its modulation is accompanied by changes in motor cortical activity reflecting E/I balance. To this end, we used a closed-loop paradigm in which real-time changes in the sensorimotor 1/f slope during neurofeedback trigger transcranial magnetic stimulation to probe intracortical circuits in the primary motor cortex. We found lower facilitatory effects in the steeper 1/f state than in both the flatter state and at rest, despite no significant between-state differences in 1/f-adjusted band power. These findings establish the physiological relevance of 1/f modulation with cortical states and support the contribution of intracortical E/I-related processes to the aperiodic dynamics.
